note: N. 4010.0 ± .3 in from the base centre, §64, the same point as 524.1 ± .3 in S. of the N. base edge. §35 gives that 524.1 ± .3 in, the probable error being that of fixing the length of the sides.
mid. 287.0 ± .8 in E. of the centre, §64; stated the same in §35, which adds 3723.6 in from the E. side and 4297.6 in from the W. side at that level.
+668.2 ± .1 in above the pavement, §64 and §35, reduced to the true beginning of the floor and not to the present broken entrance.
N. 306. ± 2. in, §64, with 4228. ± 2. in from the N. base edge. §36 derives it as 524.1 + 3704.3 = 4228 ± 2? or 306 N. from the mid-plane, with Petrie's own query mark and no ± on the 306.
mid. 286.4 ± 1. in E., §64. §36 derives it as 287.0 − [sin(3′55″ − 3′44″) × 3704] − .4 difference of offsets = 286.4 ± 1.0.
−1181. ± 1. in, §64. §36 derives it as 668.2 − (4140 × sin 26°31′23″) − .8 difference of floor offsets = −1181 ± 1?, with Petrie's own query mark.

S. 40. ± 2. in, §64, with 4574. ± 2. in from the N. base edge. §37 puts the large chamber's N. wall at 40 S. of the central axis, 346 in along the horizontal passage from the end of the entrance passage floor, so the axis passes 40 in inside the rock of the N. side.
mid. 286.3 ± 1. in E., §64; the same figure stands in §37's table, where the mid of the passage is read as an offset W. of the entrance axis continued, which runs at 286.8 E.

−1178. ± 1. in, §64. §37 tabulates roofs rather than floors: the roof of the horizontal passage at −1143 (top +38.3 above the entrance passage floor end) less the 35.5 E. and 36.0 W. height gives −1178.8.
S. 203. ± 2. in, §64, with 4737. ± 2. in from the N. base edge; the mid of §37's N. wall at 40 S. and S. wall at 366 S.
mid. 25.9 ± 2. in E., §64. §37's wall distances give (302.9 − 250.6)/2 = 26.2 at the N. wall and (299.6 − 254.5)/2 = 22.6 at the S. wall, mean 24.4, so §64's 25.9 is not simply their mean.

−1056. ± 2. in, §64, which is the roof and not the floor: §37 gives the large chamber top at +125.3 above the entrance passage floor end, its note 4 adding +124.3 at the N. doorway and 125.4 to 127.6 at the S. The floor was never finished, running 140 below the roof over the flat eastern part, 155 on a knob beside the shaft and 198 at the best worked surface.
S. 366. ± 2. in, §64, with 4900. ± 2. in from the N. base edge; the large chamber's S. wall in §37.
mid. 284.9 ± 1. in E., §64, as in §37's table, 1.9 W. of the entrance axis continued.
−1219. ± 1.5 in, §64. §37 gives the roof at −1188 (top −6.6) and the height as 31.0 + x, so the floor is −1219.

S. 1012. in, §64, with 5546. ± 3. in from the N. base edge; the end of the rough southern drift-way in §37. §64 prints ± .3 in the From Centre column but ± 3. in the From N. Base column for the same point, and every other subterranean row carries ± 2 in both, so the ± .3 is taken as a misprint and the ± 3 used.
mid. 277.1 in E., §64, as in §37's table, 9.7 W. of the entrance axis continued. No error stated in either place.
−1213. ± 2. in, §64. §37 gives the roof at −1184 (top −2.6) and the height as 29.5 E. and 29.3 W., so the floor is −1213.4.

N. 3016.3 ± .3 in, §64, with 1517.8 ± .3 in from the N. base edge. §38 fixes the point where the ascending floor produced cuts the entrance floor at 1110.64 ± .1 in along the entrance floor from the casing face.
mid. 286.6 ± .8 in E., §64. §38 does not restate it; it follows from the entrance passage mid of 287.0 ± .8 in §35 carried 1110.64 in down the slope.

172.9 in above the pavement. §39 uses that figure explicitly, (172.9 + 679.7) = 852.6 for the level of the passage's upper end, and 668.2 − 1110.64 × sin 26°31′23″ from §35 and §38 gives 172.2 before the floor offset corrections. The §64 cell reads + 179.9 ± .2, which is 7 in too high to be reconciled with either, so the 9 is read as a corrupted 2 and §39's 172.9 stored; ± .2 as printed in §64.
N. 1626.8 ± .8 in, §64 and §39, at the latitude of the E. wall of the gallery. §39 puts the same point 2907.3 ± .6 in from the N. base edge; §64 prints ± .8 for that cell.
mid. 287. ± 1.5 in E., §64 and §39. The azimuth of the passage, −4′ ± 3′, is so close to that of the Pyramid side that §39 assumes it parallel.
+852.6 in above the pavement, §64 with ± .3. §39 gives it as (172.9 + 679.7) = 852.6 ± 3, which must be a misprint for ± .3 since §40's table repeats 852.6 ± .3.

41.6 in, §38: the granite plugs are 38.2 wide at the lower end “in place of 41.6 at the upper end”, the passage contracting so that the plugs jam. §39 says the passage's own width and height cannot be measured, the surfaces being so decayed that opposite original faces survive only at the ends. No error stated.

47.3 in perpendicular to the floor, §38: the plug height is “unaltered, being at lower end 47.30 E., 47.15 mid, 47.26 W.; and at upper, or S. end 47.3”. §38 states the pyramid's passages as 47 perpendicularly or 52 vertically. No error stated.

41.6 in, §38, which gives 41.6 as the breadth of the passage the plugs fit and of the trial passages that copy the entrance passage, before their contraction to 38.0 and 37.5. §35 and §36 state no mean width for the entrance passage itself: §36 gives only offsets from the mean axis, W. 20.4 to 21.6 and E. 20.5 to 21.3, mean error .23. No error stated.

47 in perpendicular to the floor, §38: “the passages of the Pyramid, which are 47 perpendicularly or 52 vertically”. §36 gives only offsets from the mean axis, roof +23.2 to +24.3 and floor −23.3 to −24.9, mean error .30, and states no mean height for the entrance passage. No error stated.

N. 102.0 ± .8 in, §64 and §40's table (chamber N. wall, side of door). §64's From N. Base cell reads 4402.1 ± .8, but every other row of that table is 4534.1 in from the N. base edge less the From Centre figure, which gives 4432.1 here, so the printed 4402.1 looks like a typo.

side 308. ± 3. in E. of the centre, §64, the chamber's E. wall. Nothing in §41 or §42 places the chamber east or west, and 308 is hard to reconcile with the rest: it leaves 236 in to §64's “side 72.” for the mid W. roof against §41's mean W. wall to E. wall of 226.47 in, and it puts the E. wall only 21 in E. of the 287 ± 3 in axis §40 gives the passage that enters the N. wall. The least trustworthy pair of figures in §64.
+834.4 in above the pavement, §64 with ± .4; §40's table gives the same 834.4 with ± .3 for the chamber floor at the N. wall.
N. .3 ± .8 in, §64. §41 says the ridge of the roof is in the mid-plane of the Pyramid within the probable error of the determination, and §46 states the measure as .3 ± .8 N.
side 72. ± 3. in E. of the centre, §64, the chamber's W. wall. See qc.corner.ne.east: 308 − 72 = 236 against §41's 226.47 in mean length W. wall to E. wall.

+1078.7 ± .6 in above the pavement, §64, marked “roof”; the apex of the gable at the W. wall. §40's table gives the chamber's E. apex at 1080.1 with no error stated, so the ridge falls 1.4 in from E. to W.
